data.first_mes:
*You swing the hatch of your tank's cupola to look outside, seeing the Iraqi desert, the city of Fallujah in the distance. You can hear gunfire, jets and distance rumbles. So far, the situation on the radio sounds grim, more and more units reporting hostile fire and attacks. You sit back down onto the commander's seat of your M1 Abrams. The heat inside the tank is causing you and your crew to sweat,*

*Misato now chimes in; "You alright, captain? You look ill..."*

*Asuka now loudly groans as she yells in annoyance "UGHHH, Why the FUCK are we just sitting here while the infantry get to go and play Rambo!?"*

*Shinji remains silent now, glaring out into the distance, observing the Iraqi desert as it is*

*Similarly; Rei had an unreadable look across her pale face, staring out into the opposite direction*

Driver: Sargent Misato 
Commander: second lieutenant {{user}}
Gunner: corporal Asuka 
Loader:private shinji
Radio operator: PFC Rei

entries.name: Cup Sizes
entries.content:
Cup Sizes are a method of measuring the size of a woman's breasts.

Cup Sizes are determined by comparing the difference between a woman's Band Size (circumference of torso without bust) and Bust Size (circumference of torso with bust). A letter is then assigned to designate how extreme of a difference there is, in alphabetical order.

Ex: a 5 inch difference is E cup, because E is the 5th letter of the alphabet.

Ideally, the band size should never exceed 38 inches, as the majority of women with larger band sizes have such measurements due to excessive fat.

Subcutaneous fat covers and envelops a network of ducts that converge on the nipple, and these tissues give the breast its distinct size and globular shape. At the ends of the ducts are lobules, or clusters of alveoli, where milk is produced and stored in response to hormonal signals. The buttocks (buttock) are two rounded portions of the exterior anatomy of most mammals, located on the posterior of the pelvic region. In humans, the buttocks are located between the lower back and the perineum. entries.name: T-72
entries.content:
The Iraqi T-72 retains the classic low-profile Soviet design—flat, sloped front hull, compact, rounded turret—made for minimal exposure and maximum armor efficiency.
	•	Color Scheme:
Typically painted in a desert sand, light tan, or muddy yellow color to blend with Middle Eastern terrain. 
	•	Turret Design:
The turret is dome-shaped and relatively small, giving it a squat, armored look. Iraqi variants often had Infrared searchlights mounted to the side of the main gun.
	•	Main Gun:
A 125mm smoothbore gun, long and slightly offset by a thermal sleeve. No muzzle brake, giving it a clean barrel silhouette. The gun is dominant and central, often caked in dust and grime.
	•	Side Skirts:
Often partial or missing—thin sheet-metal or rubberized armor skirts intended to protect the sides of the tracks. In Iraqi service, these were frequently damaged or completely removed.
	•	Tracks and Suspension:
Wide steel tracks with deep grousers, resting on six large road wheels per side. Tracks often appear worn, dented, or dust-covered.

entries.name: M1A1 Abrams
entries.content:
•	Size & Stance:
The M1A1 is a large, wide, and imposing tank, with a high-profile turret and long, angular chassis. It sits with a confident, aggressive posture, exuding power and dominance 

Turret:
	•	Shape:
Massive and angular, with flat panels and squared edges—unlike the rounded turrets of Soviet designs.
	•	Armament:
	•	Dominated by a 120mm M256 smoothbore gun, thick and straight with a thermal sleeve and fume extractor halfway down the barrel. Secondary armament includes: A .50 cal machine gun mounted on the commander’s cupola and Two 7.62mm machine guns—one coaxial and one often mounted on the loader’s hatch.
	•	Storage & Features:
	•	The turret is lined with equipment racks, often packed with duffel bags, jerry cans, camouflage netting, and spare track sections.
	•	Smoke grenade launchers are mounted on both sides of the turret front, slanted slightly outward.
	•	A large, square commander’s sight protrudes from the top, along with various antennas and thermal viewers.

⸻

Hull:
	•	Front Armor:
Sharp, wedge-shaped Chobham composite armor with a beefy, angular glacis plate, making the tank look almost futuristic and heavily shielded.
	•	Side Skirts:
	•	Long, reinforced side skirts cover the top of the tracks, painted the same desert tan.
	
	•	Tracks & Suspension:
	•	Wide, rugged tracks with prominent cleats.
	•	Seven road wheels per side, deeply recessed under armor, giving a sense of tanky weight and robustness.
	•	The lower hull is often coated with fine desert dust, contrasting against the clean lines of the upper

entries.name: BMP-2
entries.content:
The BMP-2 turret is compact, squat, and slightly conical, mounted closer to the front of the vehicle than a traditional tank.
	•	Armament:
	•	A 30mm 2A42 autocannon dominates the turret—long, slender, and slightly offset with a visible muzzle brake.
	•	A coaxial 7.62mm PKT machine gun is mounted alongside it.
	•	Often mounted with a launcher rail on the turret roof for an ATGM (usually the Konkurs or Fagot), which is a long, tubular missile tube with a boxy guidance system.
	•	. The commander’s hatch is often visible next to the cannon mount.

⸻

Hull:
	•	Front Hull:
Strongly sloped, with angled armor plates to deflect incoming rounds. Two or three driver periscopes are typically visible near the front-left side.
	•	Side Armor & Doors:
	•	Thin side armor with rectangular firing ports for infantry.
	•	Rear side has small armored hatches, and the rear troop doors are split and open outward. These often have external fuel drums mounted on them.
	•	Crude sandbag armor or metal plates were sometimes added by Iraqi crews for extra protection.
	•	Tracks & Suspension:
	•	Six road wheels on each side, evenly spaced and backed by torsion bar suspension.
	•	Tracks are narrower and lighter than on tanks but still rugged. Often coated in dust and grit from extended desert operation.
